beginner.problemText: A college is studying how long students take to commute to campus. Let X be the commute time for one randomly selected student, in minutes. The population mean is 42 minutes. The population standard deviation is 12 minutes. The population is skewed right. A random sample has 36 students. Let X̄ be the average commute time for these 36 students. Use the Central Limit Theorem to set up the sampling distribution of X̄. Estimate the probability that the sample mean is less than 39 minutes. Write one sentence that explains the probability in this college context.

Uses “average” before “sample mean” to support accessibility.
Avoids formulas, z-scores, and computed standard errors.

beginner.problemText: At Doñana National Park in Spain, donkeys help manage weeds as part of conservation monitoring. Let X be the amount of gardenweed eaten, in grams, by one randomly selected donkey during one grazing session. For all such grazing sessions, the mean amount eaten is 1100 grams, and the standard deviation is 100 grams. A sample of 22 donkeys is observed. Let X̄ be the average amount of gardenweed eaten for this sample. Use the Central Limit Theorem to set up the normal model for X̄. Estimate the probability that the average gardenweed consumption is between 1080 and 1144 grams.

Uses “average” before relying on the term “sample mean.”
Keeps the conservation context clear without adding unnecessary detail.

intermediate.problemText: In a conservation monitoring study at Doñana National Park in Spain, researchers record gardenweed consumption during donkey grazing sessions. Using the sampling distribution of the sample mean and a normal approximation, find the probability that the average gardenweed consumption is between 1080 and 1144 grams.
